description: Add graded prism boundary layers at a wall patch (snappyHexMesh addLayers): compute per-wall-point inward normal, move the interior mesh's wall points inward by the total layer thickness, and fill the gap with N stacked prism cells per wall face (graded first_thickness * expansion^i). No hanging nodes (1:1 with wall faces). Needs a general assembler VolumeMesh::from_cell_faces (match shared faces by point-set) + cells_faces (invert owner/neighbour). New layers module: add_boundary_layers(mesh, patch, n, first_thickness, expansion). v1: a single closed wall patch. V&V: a box + N layers preserves EXACT volume (repartition), validate closed, cell count grows by N*n_wall_faces, the new outer wall sits at the original wall position, prism cells present.
title: cfmesh: prism boundary layers (near-wall inflation)

description:
Filed after hours (2026-08-11 23:55 +08) as a record only, per the CLAUDE.md
working-hours guardrail. No code was written and none should be until the next
active window.

## Ask

Give `outram-foam-basic-lib`'s numerical-math kernels an optional **hybrid
execution backend**: the same API can run serial, multi-CPU (rayon), or on the
GPU (wgpu), chosen at run time, with the serial CPU path always present as the
reference implementation.

Scope named by the maintainer:

- root finding
- golden-ratio (golden-section) search / 1-D minimisation
- matrix solutions (LDU + Krylov + dense)
- numerical integration
- numerical differentiation

## Why here

These are Layer 1-3 building blocks (`polynomial/`, `math/`, `matrix/`,
`krylov/`, `ldu_matrix/`, `ode/`), so every solver crate above
(`outram-foam-appbuilder-lib`, `outram-foam-turbulence-lib`, `tampines`,
GeN-Foam) inherits the acceleration without its own GPU code. The workspace
already has a wgpu precedent in `njoy-outram-park-fork` (Faddeeva/WMP kernels)
and `outram-mc-libs` (`op-u6s`, `op-9s8`), so the backend-enum + CPU-fallback
shape is established rather than novel.

## Constraints that bind this work

- **Hybrid means dispatch, not two APIs.** One public entry point per kernel;
  the backend is a parameter. The batch size / problem size decides whether GPU
  dispatch is worth the transfer, and that policy is explicit and documented,
  not hidden.
- **Enum dispatch, no trait objects, no `Box`, no lifetime params** (workspace
  Rust design rules). `ComputeBackend { Serial, CpuMulti, Gpu }`.
- **Android/Termux hard rule.** wgpu and any GPU-only test/example must be
  target-gated so `cargo check -p outram-foam-basic-lib --all-targets --target
  aarch64-linux-android` still passes and a native Termux build still works.
  Default features must stay Android-clean. Relates to epic `op-zfr`.
- **`uom` typing is not to be stripped** to get data onto the GPU. Convert at
  the buffer boundary and convert back; the public signature stays typed.
- **CPU is the oracle.** Every GPU kernel needs a parity gate against the
  serial CPU path with a stated tolerance, and the docs must carry both the
  methodology and the measured numbers (workspace V&V documentation rule). f32
  GPU accuracy is a known open question elsewhere in the workspace (`op-0nh`)
  — do not assume f64 on the GPU.
- **No human V&V is claimed** by any of this until the maintainer signs off.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-12: f32 GPU accuracy accepted for now, to be carried as a documented caveat in each kernel's docs and in the crate README rather than solved. See the note on op-yvj.4.7 for what the caveat must state. Also confirmed: the batched/lane-per-cell formulation is the right shape for these kernels -- batch N independent problems, keep single-problem solves serial.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: hybrid wgpu/multi-CPU backend for the numerical-math kernels
